utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Alexis Demirdjian, Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We are given to understand that there are some matter to be raised before the witness takes the stand again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, a very quick submission by Stanisic Defence. We find with concern that the disclosure violations are becoming a real problem in this case. Your Honours should understand first and foremost that the OTP investigator seized almost all documents for Bosnia-Herzegovina in period between 1996 and 2004. Some of them were copied and returned to archives, but obviously a significant number has not and is in the OTP vaults or database. We are not allowed access to these documentation or have possibility to search it. This violation that I'm talking about it the third one since the start of the Defence case 8 days ago. In all three cases that we -- of violation we brought up to Your Honours attention, the OTP acknowledged the failure to disclose documents in accordance with Rule 68 and claimed that its due to black holes or search engines failures or alike. The Doboj disclosure seems especially problematic. Yesterday we were assured by the Office of the Prosecutor that their repeated searches didn't produce anything in relation to the document we were discussing in court, only to disclose to us one of the -- one of the -- the most important documents from that file, after two and a half hours, after we finished the examination-in-chief of the current witness. What is even more worrisome, in our opinion, is the fact that the document disclosed yesterday is actually the document signed by the accused Stanisic. According to ERN number we think that the document comes from the seizure of MUP RS archives, but we can only speculate as we don't have the precise information. It is very unlikely, I must say, that OTP given the time that the accused Stanisic was indicted in 2005 did not search the vast documentation in their possession with the key word being name of the accused and especially if it comes from the MUP RS seizure. For that reason, we cannot accept the black hole or search engine failure explanation. The Defence is preparing a motion to illustrate on how many times we requested the disclosure of relevant material sometimes specific and sometimes less specific, but in any case specific enough to assume on information received from the OTP that such document does not exist. Now, after start of the Defence case we see that it in fact does exist. So what does that speak of fairness in this case? To quote Stakic Appeals Chamber judgement of 22nd March 2006, paragraph 188: "The disclosure of material pursuant to Rule 68 is fundamental to the fairness of the proceedings before the Tribunal. The consideration of fairness must be the overriding factor in any determination whether the governing rule has been breached." Now, Your Honours, we come to the relief and remedy. I'm really honestly wondering is there a relief for the Defence at all. Namely, we asked a number of times and keep asking for the material to be disclosed. At the same time, Office of the Prosecutor has a strict obligation under the rules to disclose to us the material and yet in only eight days since the start of the Defence case we have three serious violations of disclosure. I'm also extremely concerned and I wonder if in this situation the Defence can continue presentation of the Defence case as the documents keep popping up. Thank you very much. That was my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. Mr. Krgovic do you have anything to say before I call on Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We support the motion by Mr. Stanisic and in order to avoid similar situations in the future during our Defence case, we are about to submit a proposal with the specific request to the Prosecutor detailing what we want them to disclose to us. We still have some documents that we haven't received. Our Defence case is going to begin a little later, but we are now working on a special request for the Prosecutor in which we are going to specify the documents we want to see and also the collections of documents to which they belong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I may, Ms. Korner. Mr. Zecevic, the -- Mr. Krgovic used the word "motion" and then later on he explained what he proposes to do in terms of the specific relief that he would formulate. What I'm not clear on and what may be helpful before Ms. Korner responds is whether you are -- whether you intend to yourself formulate a specific relief or whether we are to divine from the observations that you made some relief in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I was trying to put the Chamber on notice that we are filing a motion. At this moment I'm -- I honestly don't know what the relief would be acceptable for us and that is why I brought it up as I did without specifically asking for a specific relief. But we will do that in our motion today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, I must have missed that. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, can I deal with the assertion that was made that OTP investigators seized almost all documents for Bosnia-Herzegovina in the period pre-1996 and 2004. As Your Honours have seen through even this one witness that is simply not the case, and it's a matter I propose to deal with at some stage with the witness. Second, yesterday the matter arose of this disciplinary letter involving a man named Solaja and there was a discussion about what this was all about. And we did a quick check to see if with that document we had the file. We do not have the file. However, we searched on the name of the police officer who was disciplined later yesterday or during the course of indeed while the trial was still going on and what came up, and I think we better have a look at it on the screen, was this document, and you need to go, I think, to the second page. It's actually -- we haven't had it translated yet, though we're hoping to get it translated within the next couple of weeks, but from having had a B/C/S reader look at it, it's the decision of Mico Stanisic in respect of the disciplinary appeal. And a rough translation, a rough estimate of what it says is that it's Mico Stanisic's 21st of December, 1992 decision dismissing Solaja's appeal listing as the offences: Taking a golf car, taking IDs from a Serb family, and trying to transfer three women with the last name Mandic - and the last names are given - and one man with the last name Maric, so that's Mandic and Maric, to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia using forged ID cards. So it appears to be people smuggling as well as stealing cards from a Serb family. The query that of course the same thing Mr. Zecevic raised I raised why wouldn't this turn up on the search that we clearly did on the name Mico Stanisic, and the reason I am told is as follows: When these documents are seized and scanned it's done by OCR, I think that's optical character recognition or that's how you find them. If, as is in this document, you've got the signature like that written over the typed signature it will not come up, whatever search terms you put in, and the only way of pulling such a document out is apparently by doing ... Sorry. I've now been given last moment information, Your Honours. Anyhow, that -- that's, but having said that, I've now been told -- right. In fact, somewhat to my surprise having launched into this explanation I'm told that it was disclosed to Defence on the 1st of April, 2010 in batch -- we don't know what the batch number is. It's on a CD given to the Defence on the 1st of April, 2010. And it's also on EDS. It was in fact -- right. Okay. Apparently on a Stanisic specific EDS, but I'm not saying that -- as I've said before, I agree that where we have documents that should be disclosed under any rule, we'll disclose them and we don't rely on EDS but it is there, but in fact somewhat to my surprise that was disclosed. But in any event Your Honour, that is one of the problems. Now, we didn't realise it was disclosed because it came up, we got at it by doing a search on, as I say, on the perpetrator rather than on Stanisic. And the reason it was disclosed then is in fact this document comes from the Banja Luka MUP photocopied, no originals taken, in April of 2009. Yeah. So it is a recent -- we've been doing a number of recent revisiting of various archives, I say recent, I mean a couple of years ago, and that was one of them. So it's a very recently obtained document, the original remains with the Banja Luka MUP archives, and as I say, after only having been told we haven't disclosed it yesterday so that's why we've disclosed it, we have in fact disclosed it. However, it is still -- I'm afraid it is still a problem when you are searching on these OCRs, and I'm afraid it is something that's going to keep on recurring because particularly if documents are badly scanned then a search engine will miss it. The earlier ones referred to by Mr. Zecevic, I accept -- I explained why we hadn't disclosed the earlier Bjelosevic documents because they turned up in a different section which we should have checked, that was our fault, but equally as is absolutely plain, Mr. Zecevic obviously had these documents himself, most of them were referred to in the interview by Mr. Bjelosevic and we weren't asked for them but I dealt with that, so I'm just dealing with this document at the moment. Your Honour, additionally we've had this morning a further request, allegedly under Rule 66(B) from the Defence which we will deal with separately. I can say straightaway it is unlikely that we will comply with all the requests because effectively it's the matter I raised yesterday -- not yesterday, whenever we had the legal argument last week; namely, that the Defence effectively are now asking for sight of all documents that we propose to use in cross-examination and we will be resisting that. So Your Honours, I hope that's the explanation I can give. As it turns out I don't blame Mr. Zecevic because we said we were disclosing it because we didn't do a proper check, but in fact we are not in any disclosure violation over this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So in sum where we are is that in terms of the principles there is and indeed there could be no division between counsel on opposite sides as to what the principles involved are. The practical operations would, as Ms. Korner has indicated, have to be determined on a case by-case basis and no doubt there will be continue to be complaints and the Chamber will have to rule on the particular motions and/or complaints as they arise, and depending on what the particular circumstances are, the Chamber would, of course, determine and apply the relevant sanctions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just say something because it's becoming a habit and not just in this Trial Chamber but in others for sanctions to be demanded against the Prosecution for what are said to be violations of the rules. I [indiscernible] recognised, A, the difficulty that Your Honours have pointed out, and also that we don't sit on documents however much we know it's going to cause problems for us. If we find documents, we disclose them. And that's the reality and I hope that will be accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, if there is nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just -- totally different subject but it goes back to proof of death matters that we discussed, I think, at the first day. Your Honours, we just received a further two to three hundred death certificates for people listed on our indictment and exhumation documents. They of course will have to be logged and which will take a couple of weeks and then reviewed. Then we've got to get them disclosed and translations produced, so we decided rather than filing separate motions we'll wait until we've got them all together and everything has been disclosed to the Defence, so that's going to take a few more weeks now I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: This proof of death business strikes me, no pun intended, as being a Banquo's ghost.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, continually reappearing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Would the usher please escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, good morning to you. Again there were certain procedural matters which have delayed the continuation of your cross-examination by Mr. Krgovic. We'll be now in a position to continue, and I would remind you you are still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bjelosevic. Yesterday we were discussing the meeting on the 11th of July in Belgrade and you answered my questions about it. During your interview, you mentioned two other meetings with Mr. Zupljanin during the relevant period. The first one was on the 1st of July in Teslic. You were wounded on that occasion, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You remember the action by Mr. Radulovic, you came there to see what was going on and then, as you explained, you were attacked by mistake and your ribs were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then you invited Mr. Zupljanin to come with Colonel Stevilovic to explain what was going on and Mr. Zupljanin arrived at Teslic on your invitation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I insisted that Mr. Zupljanin and Colonel Stevilovic arrive because it was a shock for me, I didn't know what was going on, and I wanted the relevant people to be there so that we could all see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, Mr. Radulovic said and Stojan Zupljanin confirmed that that particular action was planned in Banja Luka and that you were not informed about the plan for this action pursuant to an order by Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During that meeting it was established that some of the people who were there had false ID purporting that they belonged to the Security Services Centre in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was about the supplemental IDs, that's how we used to call them. And then we found that those IDs were false. That's also the first time that I saw those IDs and some other documents such as the order by Colonel Simic by which a group of military policemen was sent to Teslic and other things as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One of the charges against the group Mice was the fact that they falsely represented themselves to be authorised officials, so besides various crimes against Muslims and Croats, they were also charged with false representation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that that's true. I think I was informed at a meeting about the contents of their indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The following meeting that you mentioned was in Banja Luka on the 9th of September. Mr. Zupljanin, investigative judge, and the prosecutor from Teslic were present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I insisted on this meeting. As time went on, I found some new facts and that is why I requested this meeting. The meeting was held on the 9th of September and was attended by those people that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You wanted a thorough investigation because you wanted to find out who sent those people and how it came that you find yourself -- found yourself in this embarrassing situation, you simply wanted to clear your name, you wanted to prove to everybody that you had nothing to do with this group and their arrival at Teslic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. In the meantime I had found out that in early morning hours of the 1st of July, two young men were killed in that action. And I also wanted that to be mentioned at the meeting. I proposed that the investigation should be expanded and that it should include the issue of responsibility for the death of those two young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned two people who were killed. One from the Mice group and another one --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember there was one from the Doboj group, his name was Gostic, and the one from Teslic I think was called Sjecanin [phoen] or something like that. And I thought that this should have been investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify, it was two Serbs who were killed, one belonged to the group that was attacking the Mice and the other one from the Doboj group?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those two young men lost their lives in that conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we heard that one of them was killed from close by and that he was trying to protect himself and there was a gun-shot wound on his hand?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was another thing that persuaded me that I should do something about it. During the on-site investigation, I think that there was also an autopsy, but I think that when they were simply looking at the dead body, they saw that the bullet went through the hand, that the shot came from close by which means that the victim was trying to protect his body from the killer. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At that time in July the relations between you and Mr. Zupljanin were not very good precisely because of this event. We could say that they were not as good as they had been before?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. There were problems between the two of us. Especially when Mr. Zupljanin arrived with Colonel Stevilovic, I asked whether Radulovic carried out this action with his approval and why I was not informed about it. I don't know that even today, and all right, I don't really have to know that; however, as a man, as a chief of a centre, I was offended that it all went the way it went and I received no information about it, and it turned out I was quite naive. I expected to be informed about what happened, I arrived there, and in the end I almost lost my life, so, yes, there were problems between the two of us. I had significant reservations towards Mr. Zupljanin in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you think about the possibility that you were not informed because of the secrecy, because there was the danger of leaking of information? Mr. Savic, the man in Doboj, was concerned that maybe there could be a leak of information and that could be the reason why you were not informed about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As time went by I changed my position about all this, but at that particular moment I was offended and frustrated, and later on when things fell into place, if I could say so, yes, I think that people had every right to suspect me as well, but I think that later on everything was clarified and that all suspicions were dispelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. These are all my questions. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said yesterday or the day before, if I may, I'd like to ask some questions now. I don't think they will take beyond the adjournment at 10.25 and then adjourn the rest of cross-examination until the witness returns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So you will open your cross-examination now and continue when the witness returns.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, you'll see the reason why I'm asking these questions now, they are basically to do with documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, when the investigators met you in 2004 you were head of the analytical department in Doboj CSB; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the public security centre in Doboj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you still in that position?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In 2004 you had only been approached potentially as a witness for the Krajisnik case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, you were asked at the beginning of the 2004 interview when you had your lawyer present, Mr. Simic -- forgive me. Well, I should put it correctly. What you were asked by the investigator in 2004, Mr. Sebire was: "In the past have you been contacted by any representative of a Defence team working at the Tribunal for any case before the Tribunal?" This is page 12 of the first interview. And you said: "No -- yes, actually there was a memo that came to the" typed up as the PSC, but I assume that means the CSB, "referring to the possibility that someone could be involved in the Defence of Mr. Krajisnik." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that that was the contents of the conversation and that a document was shown to me, but I do remember that Goran Neskovic, I think, mentioned the Defence of Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In any event, I don't think it matters much, but that's -- you weren't shown a document you were asked and that was the reply you gave, and just to complete that part, you said you weren't in a position to assist in the Defence of Mr. Krajisnik. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely how it went, but it is quite possible that something like that was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. When you were seen in 2009 you had already been asked by the Defence of Mr. Stanisic to be a witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before I was invited to the interview in 2009, I had already been contacted by the Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. That's all right, I'm going to ask you some further questions about that, but that's what I want to know. Can you tell the Court, please, when were you first contacted?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the first time but I remember that I gave some sort of preliminary statement, maybe one year earlier, one year before I spoke to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you give that preliminary statement to Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you asked to sign that statement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that really.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of that statement with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you shown a copy of that statement at any stage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So that's -- you saw Mr. Cvijetic, you made a preliminary statement to him. Who else did you see from the Defence team of Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When? In what period?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Between the first time you saw them which was you think in about 2008, because you say it was about a year before you saw us, between then and now, how often have you met with members of the Stanisic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't remember. I used to meet Mr. Zecevic. Now, how many times he contacted me, I really don't remember that. I didn't think about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you meet him in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade and Banja Luka, and here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As you were employed presumably you made a note in your appointments diary of your meetings with Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I made no note.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about notes. I'm asking you whether you recorded either in your personal diary or your appointments diary which you presumably keep as part of your employment of the number of meetings that you had with Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you personally have no record of the number of meetings or when they took place?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you met with Mr. -- was it always Mr. Zecevic or was it Mr. Cvijetic or somebody else from the team that you met?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time, as I said, it was Mr. Cvijetic. The second time, Mr. Zecevic. And we also met in Banja Luka and both Mr. Zecevic and Mr. Cvijetic were there, and then also here before the beginning of the trial I met with both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, that you came here before you started to testify. I'm concerned only with the earlier meetings. At those meetings was Mr. Zecevic or Mr. Cvijetic or anybody else taking notes of what was being said?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke about certain documents, and I think that they were making some notes during the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you asked to sign any kind of statement or notes that had been made of what you had said?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was only once that I gave the preliminary statement that I mentioned. I think that I signed that statement. As for the notes, I don't remember. I think we looked at some documents but I'm not sure that I signed any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn next to your meeting with Mr. Krgovic. When was the first time that you met Mr. Krgovic, or anybody from the Zupljanin Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Banja Luka I think in the spring, but we only met there, we were introduced, we didn't have any conversation about the facts from the Defence of Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who introduced you to Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you had no conversation about any of the Zupljanin side of the case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that occasion, no, not during that meeting. We were only introduced. They told me that they represent Mr. Zupljanin and then they spent a short time there and went away. We did not mention the facts related to the Defence of Mr. Zupljanin on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When did you mention the facts concerned with Mr. Zupljanin? When did you discuss the matters concerning Mr. Zupljanin with Mr. Krgovic or anybody else from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a brief conversation here, here in The Hague, before I began testifying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did he explain to you then what he was going to ask you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, briefly speaking he gave some contours of the general direction of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You see, until this morning, Mr. Bjelosevic, and in nearly two weeks of giving evidence, this morning is the first time that you mentioned the word "Mice" as a result of questions put to you by Mr. Krgovic. Was that a deliberate arrangement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did not mention that word this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, indeed you are quite right it was actually brought up by Mr. Krgovic. But you have not mentioned the incident in the whole of your two weeks of testimony that involved the Mice in which you were involved as well. Now, I want to know if there is a reason for that, please?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, on two occasions, Mr. Bjelosevic, when you were being asked questions by Mr. Zecevic, you explained that at the beginning of July you had been in hospital, you did not mention how it was that you came to be in hospital. Now, was that something that was arranged between you and Mr. Krgovic and Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion between you and Mr. Zecevic about what, if anything, would be asked by him in relation to the Mice?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it's pure coincidence, Mr. Bjelosevic, that it's for the first time this morning that the Judges would have realised from your testimony that you had been involved in the incident which led to the arrest of the Mice? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. What do you mean when you say that I was involved in it? I stuck to the suggestion that I received at the beginning, and that is that my answers should relate to the questions, that my answers should be brief and clear. Now this thing that you just mentioned that I was involved in it, I think that I spoke about that. I think that we spoke about it, you and I, in 2009, and I think that that's when I explained what happened, how it was that I -- how it came to be that I was there when I can of course talk about it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Bjelosevic, I'm going to come back to substantive matters on that when you return. All I'm concerned about and all I'm asking you about at the moment is whether there was any arrangement between you, Mr. Zecevic, and Mr. Krgovic that the first questions that would be asked about the Mice would come when Mr. Krgovic cross-examined you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I really think that this question was asked and it's been answered for the third time. I don't have a problem with the witness answering the question, but I think certain measures have to be applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask one final question on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When Mr. Krgovic spoke to you before you started testifying, did you discuss with him that he would ask you questions about the Mice?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What does that mean? What does "not in this way" mean?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he would pose those questions and that I would answer those questions and so on and so forth. That's not how our conversation went.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he say to you that he would be the one to ask you questions about the Mice?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you didn't realise this morning that he was going to put questions to you about the Mice, is that what you are telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe it or not, I had no idea about what questions Mr. Krgovic was going to ask because when we met here in The Hague, he told me that he would have several questions for me, that there would not be many questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So all these questions that he asked you this morning and indeed yesterday, you had no idea that he was going to ask you those questions; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is nonsense. All my questions and all his answers are also in his interview. He gave identical answers to the questions that he was asked in his interview. Now, what is the problem, the way I'm asking, what I'm asking? All the questions and all the answers are contained in the interview and Ms. Korner knows this very well. He was asked twice, he answered twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours know that I'm not asking about that. I'm asking about whether Mr. Bjelosevic was aware of which questions were going to be asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so your final answer, is Mr. Bjelosevic, you did not know what questions Mr. Krgovic was going to ask you or what topics he was going to cover?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really did not know what questions would be put. Tentatively, he gave me certain guide-lines as to the fact that what would be discussed is what had been discussed previously, but he did not say we are going to have such and such questions put to you, so that was not the preparation as it was. The structuring of the question did not happen during our conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So we moved from he didn't discuss what he was going to ask me -- sorry, I'm just going to turn up the exact words. "I had no idea about what questions Mr. Krgovic was going to ask" was -- your answer now is that he gave certain guide-lines but didn't say that he was going to put such and such a question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say which subjects would be discussed. I said that he would -- that we would go through -- that he went with me through certain things in terms of what would be discussed. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to move to a slightly different topic. In the meetings that you had with the Stanisic Defence team, did they ask you to produce documents or did you volunteer to give them documents?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a number of documents voluntarily. I can put it that way, because I understood through the conversation that these documents could be useful in proving the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off, we can barely hear the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not quite understand what you meant when you said "voluntarily."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did they ask you for any documents that you were able to get hold of that related to specific topics, or did you volunteer and say I have documents that may help you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As in the conversation in 2004, in the interview, some of the documents that I handed over to the investigators, that is how I handed over certain documents to the Defence of Mr. Stanisic, the documents that I had at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you keep -- I'll come back to records at your disposal, documents at your disposal. Did you keep a record of the documents that you handed over to the Stanisic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What you are saying, you just gave them documents without keeping any record whatsoever of the documents that you gave them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't record anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How many documents did you give them in all?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really cannot say now. I'm bound to say the truth and I cannot say things just off the cuff. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You have, as the Trial Chamber has seen, I would suggest, an almost perfect recall of events that happened 17 years ago. Are you saying that you cannot recall how many, let's just take it, was it 100, 200, 300?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When speaking of how it is that I remember certain things, not all impressions are equally important to a person and not everything leaves the same kind of deep imprint in human memory. Some things remain carved in memory and there are others that you simply consider to be unimportant or less important and you don't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let me take the figures again. Are you saying it was something in the region of 100 or less than 100?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly less but how many I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where did you get the documents from that you provided to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in different ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Explain the different ways.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are some documents that I have had since 1992. There are some documents that I received later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's start with the documents you've had since 1992. Do you mean you personally?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, the document I showed you here, that order that stood on the bulletin board, yes, that is the document from 1992. I had it since then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You explained that one. What other documents did you provide to the Defence which you personally had had since 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there are some orders of the Crisis Staff that I was to use for explaining the work of the MUP, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How many Crisis Staff documents did you have at home?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, well, what had to do with me and where I was supposed to attend meetings, and I think it was two or three documents, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And these are official documents that you were sent in your official capacity as chief of the CSB Doboj in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents were addressed to me using my name and surname. I explained how specific my work was at the time. I was not in the office all the time at the centre. For the most part I was at the command post and at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But that's not an answer to my question, and you know it isn't, Mr. Bjelosevic. Are these official documents that you were sent in your official capacity?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, the very same question he, the witness gave the answer. Yes, he did. On page 24/14: "These documents were addressed to me using my name and surname."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That's an answer, but there's an element to the question which Ms. Korner is exploring which isn't clear from what the witness has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In Serbian it sounded like an answer very clear to the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll try and make it a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sure the documents were addressed to you using your name and surname. Would you have been sent the documents about Crisis Staff meetings or decisions if you had not been chief of the CSB in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who they invited and in which capacity, but they invited me to two or three meetings and on every one of these documents what was written in pen was my name and surname and further down what I was supposed to do at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were they not, Mr. Bjelosevic, official documents which should have been kept in the records of the Doboj CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the document did not state CSB Doboj. You can have a look at these documents. It said my name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's the next question in fact that I'm going to come on to, Mr. Bjelosevic. Are you prepared either to hand over to a representative of the OTP or to bring to court when you return, copies of all documents that you personally have at home that relate to the events of 1992 when you were the chief of the CSB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we actually went through all of those documents in 2004, 2009, and now here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, what you think and what is the reality is maybe two different things. But I'm simply asking you at the moment whether you are prepared to hand over copies of all the documents which you have at home which relate to the events of 1992 whilst you were the chief of the CSB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you prepared to hands them over to an investigator from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I rephrase that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To the Sarajevo field office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The witness started to answer, please leave the opportunity to the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to say that if you wish when I return here on the 16th I will photocopy everything and bring everything I have. As a matter of fact, in 2004, and you will probably find that there, I photocopied something from my notebooks. I would like to say something here and I would like it to be fully clear: I have nothing to hide and I do not wish to hide anything. I came here to tell the truth and that is why I appear as a witness here. Let that be perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic. So -- and in fact, I was going to -- I changed because I was going to say: Are you prepared to have someone from the Sarajevo field office collect those documents in advance because otherwise it will mean a delay when you get here while we all look at the documents?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you're asking me whether I am prepared to photocopy all of this and then hand it over to someone before I actually come here? Somebody would contact me; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, someone will contact you from the Sarajevo field office, you don't have to do the photocopying, you can either give them to them, they will be returned to you, because you'll get a receipt for the documents, or you can photocopy them yourself, whichever you prefer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you said some the documents you had at home. Where else of the 92 documents or so which are on the list that the Defence have provided that you provided, where did the other documents come from?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a number of documents as photocopies while speaking to the Defence. They showed me a number of documents and they say that they received them from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. There are, according to the list we've been given, numbers of documents that were shown to you that did not come from us but came from you and you alone. Now, where did you get the documents that weren't at home?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of documents are from the book of General Lisica, or rather the books of General Lisica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Leave aside the books of General Lisica. Did you take copies of any documents from the CSB Doboj where you were working as head of the archives, or analyst?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for a number of documents, I would like to remind you that in the media 2003 I read that in Zenica there were some proceedings, roughly that's what it said in the newspapers, that there were proceedings instituted against me and they said that they didn't have my address and then I reported to the court and OTP in Zenica. I called them and I asked them what this was all about. They said to me that there was a request for carrying out an investigation and that it would be a good idea if I were to show up. I indeed went there. They read that request to me, so I saw what it was all about. When I returned, I asked for some documents that have to do with those allegations in the request for an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You mean when you returned to the CSB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned from Zenica, yes, I returned to the Doboj centre, and they said to me that there were a number of documents there that some of the documents were from there, they had them photocopied and they provided me with these copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. So some of the documents that you have provided to the Defence come from the CSB Doboj via you for the purposes of any potential Defence you have to mount; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time, I am afraid I'm going to go a little bit over the break because I still have a few question to ask about documents, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, when you say go over the break, are you suggesting that we continue beyond --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I see it's 10.25 which is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I have got about another 15, 20 minutes worth of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is there any reason why we can't do that now?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, well, no. If you want -- certainly if you want to. I thought you wanted to have the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Let me just check with the Court Officer first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The universal view is that we continue, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I am afraid actually having looked, it's going to take about another 30 minutes. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So that will be 45.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I mean I've just seen there's one whole area that I omitted --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be practical, we need to talk about the scheduling as well, so therefore I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think for the convenience of the accused who are in the care of the security officers, so we'll take the break and come back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I want to deal with documents at the Doboj CSB, please. You told us that you got some documents from Doboj CSB for the purposes of a potential defence. The archives in the Doboj CSB, where exactly are they located?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which room it is where the archive is, but it must be somewhere in the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am sorry --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it's somewhere in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You've worked for Doboj CSB now for something like 17 or 18 years -- no, sorry, 20 years. Are you telling us you don't know in which room the archives are kept?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first, esteemed Prosecutor, I don't work that long in the security services centre in Doboj. I worked there until the beginning of 1994 when I went to Bijeljina. After that, I spent a period of time in Sarajevo, then I went back to Bijeljina and also to Brcko and Banja Luka. And then in 2000 -- I don't remember exactly which year I returned to the Doboj CSB, and I think that the archive is in the basement, in the same building where the station and the centre are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this is just a marginal digression, is it right that the SJB Doboj and the CSB Doboj since 1991 or maybe before have always been in the same building?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So the archives you think are in the basement of the CSB. Who is in charge of the archives? Name of the person, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Trust me, I don't know who is in charge of the archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You are the head of analysis and you don't know who is in charge of the archives at CSB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the person. I don't know the individual, but logically speaking it's something to do with the administrative office and it definitely should be admin and financial department or something like that. It may sound incredible to you, but I really don't know the first and the last name of the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Who is the head of the administration and financial department at the present time in Doboj CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branislav Petricevic, he was mentioned here, he used to be an inspector in the crime prevention department.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The documentation that is retained in the archives of the CSB, is that separated into each separate department or administration within the CSB? In other words, is there a separate set of binders of documents for the crime prevention department or for the financial department and so on?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is regulated by the Law on Documents and Archives. I think that's the exact name of the law. I assume that the documents are grouped according to the terms, by that I mean how long they have to be kept. There is a group of document that have to be kept for a shorter period of time, some of them for a longer period of time, and yet another permanently. So that's, I assume, is also the basis for that classification in the archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is the answer to that -- without looking at the law, you can't tell -- you can't give me the answer as to how the documents are archived?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they are sorted, but I suppose that that is the criterion. I haven't done that job. I was never involved in that and that's why I don't know. This's why I don't know the criteria. However, it seems logical to me because I know that some documents are supposed to be kept longer and some shorter time, and also, yeah, it would also be quite understandable if they were categorised according to the lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The documents that have to be kept include any dispatches sent by or received by the Doboj CSB; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know how long. I think that the dispatches -- I don't want to make a mistake, but I think that the term for keeping dispatches is three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But from what you tell us you were able to get copies of documents from 1992 in 2003?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'll read back what you said to us about the documents you said you got copies of from the CSB: "As for a number of documents," this is at page 27, line 23, "I would like to remind you that in the media in 2003 I read that in Zenica there were some proceedings" sorry, "roughly that's what it said in the newspapers, there were proceedings instituted against me, and they said they didn't have my address and I reported to the court and the OTP in Zenica" and so on and so forth. "When I returned, I asked for some documents that have to do with those allegations in the request for an investigation." "Q. You mean when you returned to the CSB Doboj? "A. When I returned from Zenica, yes, I returned to the Doboj centre, and they said to me there were a number of documents, some of the documents were from there, they had them photocopied and provided me with those copies." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was the exact interpretation, but in essence, yes, that's about it. But I don't know what your question is. That's what I didn't understand. You said that in 2003 I took documents, I don't know how. It was more of a statement than a question, that's why I didn't quite understand what you were asking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'll try again, I'm sorry, Mr. Bjelosevic. I want you to be quite clear. My understanding from that answer was that having been to Zenica in 2003 to find out what the investigation against you was about, when you came back to Doboj, you got copies of documents that were in the Doboj CSB about matters in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a number of documents. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So in 2003 certainly there were documents in the Doboj CSB, dispatches and the like, that relate to 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean suddenly? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I didn't say suddenly. I don't know where it was interpreted as suddenly, but I didn't say "suddenly." Mr. Bjelosevic, I don't want to go around the houses like this, but in 2003 were you able to have copied for your purposes documents that related to 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be -- or let me attempt to be very clear. In that request for investigation I found a number of statements and characterisations which were incorrect. I said that when it was read out to me and I stand by it today. Among other things, it said that our service did not take any steps against perpetrators of certain violent acts, murders, et cetera. And then because I remembered it and I still remember it today, that there were certain steps taken, I requested that certain data be found in the KU register. They found them and I was right. There were on-site investigations, there were investigations, there were criminal reports. We also had a chance to see a number of documents of that nature during the past few days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, the simple question was in 2003 did you receive copies of documents that related to the 1992 events?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did get a number of documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there is no reason at all that you know of why the documentation in 1992 should not still be present in the archives of the Doboj CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was checking the interpretation and it was very confusing and it didn't reflect what you said. That was the precise reason why I was doing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is there -- I will say this slowly and carefully so that there can be no mistake, I hope, in the interpretation. Is there any reason you know of why the documentation from 1992, part of which you got, should not be in the CSB Doboj? In other words, it should still all be there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you are unable to assist as to where exactly in the building that documentation is kept?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We already spoke about this. Let me repeat it in order to clarify. The documents which, according to the law on documents and archives, have to be kept permanently or, for instance, for 20 years, and if we talk about 1992, then such documents should still exist in the archive. If the terms mandated by the law are shorter and have expired, then there is no obligation to continue keeping such documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Apart from your own documents at home, apart from documents that were copied for you in the CSB, are any of the documents which you provided to the Defence from any other source?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There are no other sources. As I said, the two that I mentioned and that book where copies of the documents were published, the book by General Lisica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, in order to stop what would be a very long, boring, and time consuming exercise, we have been given a list by the Defence for Mr. Stanisic of documents which it is said you provided. I would like you to be given a copy of that list, or a copy given to VWS, because as you know you cannot communicate at all with the Defence or anybody else of that list and to mark, please, for us, which documents you got from the CSB Doboj and which documents were personal documents, and don't worry about Lisica's book because I don't think any of them on there have anything to do with Lisica's book. And I would like you to do that, please, before you return. Next, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. Ms. Korner, the documents, the documents that you just mentioned has got the 65 ter numbers, not in the world can the witness know what the 65 ter number is, the particular document. Maybe you can print out all these documents and then give it to the witness so he can mark them and explain where he got them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, he actually has a full binder which he has been using all the way through of all the documents that were used, so I suggest he takes that with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the binder that was used with the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which he has been using to give evidence when he was giving evidence in chief which has got all the documents, that I understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, but that doesn't contain all the documents we listed. Because the binder contains only the documents that I intended to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, slight waste of time, but my understanding was the list that we got we asked for a list of the documents which were in the Defence binders which had been provided by this witness. Do I understand there are -- this includes documents that are not in the Defence binders, because that's -- my understanding was he used only ones in the Defence binders?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it is my mistake. They should all be in the binder. That's what Ms. Savic explained to me. So we will provide the binders to the witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, well, it's quite clear there are other documents that aren't in the binders from what we are being told, but in the absence of the Defence handing them over, there's not much I can do about that. And, Your Honours, in fact the simplest -- and I've marked my list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bjelosevic --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. There's a clean copy of the list which was provided which we'll hand over now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bjelosevic, you mentioned your own notebook. As you rightly point out, on the second day of the 2004 interview, you turned up with three photocopied pages of a notebook that you yourself kept during the period of meetings you attended. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you still have that notebook?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I would like you, please, to hand over the whole notebook to whoever turns up from the Sarajevo field office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in parenthesis, can I say I've been asked whether a representative of the Defence could be -- or not been asked it's been put to me that a representative of the Defence should be present. No objection at all. We'll notify the Defence of when or, in fact, Mr. Bjelosevic is going to have to notify the field office. Your Honours, all I'd say is of course that no communication can be held between the members of the Defence and Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We are not seeking one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In that case I'd ask you to hand over, please, the notebook relating to 1991 and 1992, please. The whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. The Chamber is just proposing that perhaps the simplest solution would be to have Mr. Bjelosevic hand over the documents and the notebooks and whatever else there is to be handed over to a representative from the VWS so that the VWS can then pass the documents on to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly. Your Honours, if VWS agree to this, then I don't know whether they are prepared to do that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But as far as we are informed, the VWS does have personnel in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So that would be the easiest and the simplest solution to this little technicality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I will -- in that case, obviously we'll leave the finer points of the arrangement for outside court, but Mr. Bjelosevic needs to communicate with the VWS in Sarajevo. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you keep a war diary when you were in the military, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one more question, if you'd permit me, before I answer your question. Is somebody going to contact me from that field office or the interpretation that I received was that I should contact them, so what is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The office will contact you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not have a war diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you give us, please, the dates in 1992 when you were performing the military duties that you have talked about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dates. Already in April I became engaged with the military in a sense. In that period, the area of Derventa, Brod, Odzak, Samac had already been cut off, war was already going in Samac, and at that time I was already making visits to the command and the garrison in Derventa. Then there was the forward command post of the 1st Corps command, it changed its location on several occasions, but more frequent visits and later on the engagement that was sometime beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Look, Mr. Bjelosevic, you've got a perfect memory virtually for other dates. I want the exact dates, please, when you say you were performing military duties?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you in my answer. I told you how it all began.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you able to give us the precise dates when you were actually performing military duties under the command of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a specific situation. It's one thing when you receive a direct order appointing you to a certain duty. And it's a different thing when you co-operate and partake in command in relation to certain issues. One could say that the engagement in the military begins sometime at the beginning of May when the command post was in the village of Strpce near Prnjavor. From that point on I was present there every day. However, I emphasise, that at the beginning of May, or rather, no, in April, it was in April that parts of the public security station in Derventa, more precisely the personnel that managed to get out, formed the station in the local community of Kalenderovci --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter heard the name right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and another one in another village. There was a commander of the milicija station, Ninko Dobrilovic and there was also a commander of the traffic police station, Pero Cvjetkovic. An attempt was made to establish a functioning service, so in that sense I was also engaged there. So in the beginning, you cannot really draw a sharp line between those two things, but I do emphasise that sometime from the beginning of May I was engaged in the command. And then sometime towards the end of May I think that the whole police was resubordinated to the army or, more precisely, they were mostly engaged in the military police. So it was a complex meshwork of obligations, co-ordination -- I don't know if you understand this particular situation. There were parts of the service outside its station, there were areas where situation should have been regulated, there were specific circumstances, and a lot of time was spent working on that. So my answer would be that it was the beginning of May or the 1st of May, I don't remember the exact date, and from that point on I was almost daily there, and then after I was appointed to a command duty, I was mostly in the field with the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. All I asked you was for the dates, but let's leave it there for the time being. What about the later period of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second half of 1992 I think that we've explained that in the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't want to stop you, Mr. Bjelosevic, but I don't want an explanation again. I'm simply asking for the dates. You told us it was April, maybe May to the end of June 1992. Were you actually performing military duties towards the end of 1992, because that's what I understood you to say. If I'm wrong, tell me now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask for the Prosecution microphone to be switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it wasn't the end of 1992. It was the end of June of 1992. It wasn't the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you do a second period of service under the military whether resubordinated or any other kind for any other period in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in November I was battalion commander. Now that we are on the subject, allow me to say one more thing. In July and August and September and October, and you could see this from the documents, we sent the milicija to the front line all the time. They were resubordinated to the military and of course I had that in mind. I contacted the commands very often. I went there to follow what was going on. I saw them out in the field, that is something that went on. But basically after this collegium, after the 11th of July, the functions and the elements of the centres are established and they have their chief and the service of the centre functioned in that period of time. It is correct that in the month of November, I was engaged for a combat duty in the Teslic front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm only interested in you, Mr. Bjelosevic, and not any of your men for the moment. Do you have your military booklet?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be kind enough, please, also to hand that over? And I say this is all going to be copied and all the originals will be given back to you to VWS with all the other documents.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you have any copies of any orders or dispatches or any material addressed to you during that first period when you say you were with the military from General Talic or any other officers under his command?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to find the order on appointment to command duty during the corridor operation. I haven't found it. Over the past few days we saw some of the documents that had arrived from the commands. I think that there are some documents that I did not testify about over the course of the past few days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, where are they? Do you mean there are documents you've given to the Defence which you haven't been asked about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think that I have some more documents, some orders that were not the subject of my testimony here over the past few days. I'll have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We are interested, as I said to you, in any documents, military, police, or whatever that emanate from 1992. That is what we would like you to hand over. Do you understand that? So that includes military.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll hand everything over to these persons who come to see me. Trust me, I have no reason to hide anything. As a matter of fact, I'll be pleased to hand them over.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Final matter I want to ask you about is this: You were asked when you first began testifying by His Honour Judge Hall whether you had testified previously before this Tribunal or before any of the courts in the countries that comprise the former Yugoslavia, and you said "No, not in these cases." Can I just ask what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood the question correctly then, it was whether I testified before this international criminal tribunal or some other international court about war crimes. That is what I meant when I said that I had not testified in those cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Very well. But you told us yesterday that you had in fact testified in the trial against Slobodan Karagic for theft?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not -- well, this is a property related crime and I don't consider that to be a question akin to war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, I accept that. As I said, Mr. Bjelosevic, I accept that you understood the question but I'm trying to get another aspect of this. When exactly was this trial against Karagic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, a rough idea, please? In the last five years, ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I really cannot recall with any precision, so take this conditionally, please, what I will say now. It might have been 2001 or 2002, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that was at the Doboj court, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the outcome of the trial? What was the verdict?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was called in as a witness and I did not follow the case. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You had no interest in the result of a case in which you had testified? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I really wasn't all that interested. I gave a statement before the court and I did not follow how things went on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that -- was the allegation in 2001 relating back to events of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The questions put to me were what does a mobilised vehicle mean and whether the vehicle in question had been mobilised by the service. That is what I testified about.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The allegation was theft of a motor vehicle, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, the witness said, I was questioned. He was not mentioning the allegations. He was questioned by the Judge. That's our system, Ms. Korner, it's different from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It really doesn't need an intervention, Mr. Zecevic. I understand perfectly the system in the former Yugoslavia, thank you very much. It's not a question of who he was questioned by.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the allegation about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I was called as a witness and that in these proceedings against Slobodan Karagic certain questions were put to me in relation to what it means when a vehicle is mobilised, and I was asked whether I remembered that that particular vehicle had been mobilised in that way. I answered the questions put to me and I really don't know how it all ended. I really do not know. You can ask the court about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm asking you as a witness to something that happened in 1992. Was this theft of a vehicle belonging to a non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a witness to the events concerned or the theft. I was asked whether I remembered that that particular vehicle had been mobilised for the needs of the service, and also what it means to mobilise a vehicle. I answered those questions to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
