utterances.text: Do you -- sorry. Do you have the faintest idea, do you know why it took from 1992 to roughly 2001 to prosecute Mr. Kasagic [sic]?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's not for me to assess that when different court cases were being resolved. I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you aware of Mr. Kasagic [sic] having been charged with any other offences arising from the events of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am really sorry. I believe Ms. Korner is using two persons. Karagic or Kasagic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Karagic, sorry, you are quite right. I made a mistake. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Karagic. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Slobodan Karagic was criminally charged for what happened in Teslic in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he ever prosecuted for that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how far the proceedings went and how they ended. I know that he was part of that criminal report together with some other persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the Mice again; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's the group. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And finally, Mr. Bjelosevic, for the time being, are there any other cases in which you have testified relating to the events of 1992 against any other accused?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember I was not called to testify anywhere in relation to what happened in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Apart from this one case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. If I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's all I ask for the present. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, you would recall the matters to which we alerted you yesterday and you indicated - that is in terms of the continuation of your testimony - and you indicated in, as a partial answer to the question earlier, and I believe the Court Officer has confirmed, and I would wish you to reconfirm this for the record, that the 16th of May would not be inconvenient to you, is that the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yesterday I spoke to my family and we looked at some other engagements that had previously been planned and that's why my phone was on when it went off yesterday and I apologise for that once again. So, yes, that particular date would do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So -- sorry you were going to say something, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I think when it comes to the Registry, I've been asked to confirm what it is exactly that Mr. Bjelosevic is supposed to be handing over to VWS, so can I just confirm so that it can be printed out, all documents in his possession, military, police, or otherwise that relate to the events of 1992. Second, his own notebook of meetings he attended in 1991 and 1992. Third, his military booklet. I think that's the complete list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So as a reminder, Mr. Bjelosevic, what Ms. Korner just said on the record would be passed on to VWS and they would have that list to you, so in other words, you don't have to -- if remember it all well and good, but you would have as an aid this list that they would provide you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that he is reminded of that he cannot communicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I intend to do that, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, we are for the reasons that I would have explained earlier, taking an extended break in this matter. Upon the rising of the Court today, we will reconvene on the 2nd of May, but your testimony is suspended -- the continuation of your cross-examination is suspended until the agreed date of the 16th of May, and with the lengthy break, I am obliged to remind you of what I said at the beginning during the adjournment the first day, that having been sworn as a witness in this matter, you cannot have any communication at all with counsel from either the Office of the Prosecution or the counsel representing either of the accused. Moreover, in such conversations as you have with persons other than counsel, please remember that you cannot discuss your testimony before the Tribunal. You are not yet released as a witness, that will come at the end of your examination-in-chief -- of the re-examination and any questions the Judges have. And with that we take the adjournment. I wish that everyone has a safe -- yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours, before we take the adjournment, I have two matters to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Shall I excuse the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: By all means, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, you will be escorted from the courtroom and we will continue with our procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I just ask you something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not quite understand what it is that I'm supposed to do with this list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That list, as I understand it - and counsel can jump in and correct me if I misstate anything - is an index, as it were, of the binder which you have been or will be handed by VWS. That list is -- will be difficult for you to follow, but what they would require you to do is to indicate from the documents which you will have in front of you the ones that you have -- could counsel, assist, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's not actually a list of [indiscernible] the binder. It's a list of the documents which are contained in the binder which it is said by the Defence was given them by Mr. Bjelosevic. And it was pointed out that just from the list it would be difficult to identify. But the documents are in the bundle and so he has just got to mark off which ones are the ones he gave. And from where. Sorry, from where he gave them -- sorry from where he acquired them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, can I just ask if the witness will be able to identify the documents in the binder from the list that you have given to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. They've got all the documents are numbered and they've got the number on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Except for the fact -- I'm sorry to interrupt, except for the fact that the document which we provided to the Office of the Prosecution is in English and, as we know, the witness doesn't speak English. Therefore, what we can do is provide the very same document in Serbian and have a copy given to the VWS so the witness knows what documents he needs to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bjelosevic --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There's no titles in any of the documents. It just gives numbers. There's nothing in English other than item or receipt of -- given by Bjelosevic. I don't follow. But, Your Honour, it may be the simplest thing is he has got the binder, if he just goes through looking at the documents and simply if he likes himself lists the tab numbers, he has got them all under tab numbers, the ones he handed over from where. Your Honour, the only other alternative is to go through a time exhausting exercise of going through each individual document ourselves with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the exercise, Mr. Bjelosevic, is for you to identify from the documents that you have the ones that would have come from the archives and the one that you would have had from your own copies or from somewhere else, so there's two or three sets of markings or indications. Can we further assist? I trust that's clear. Do you have any other questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to be sure that I understood this right. I take this and I take the list, right, and from this group of documents I am supposed to say which ones on this list are the ones that I handed over to the Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, the purpose, Mr. Bjelosevic, is to indicate on the list where you got each of these documents from. The Prosecution is asking you to identify or to indicate on the list where you got these documents from. And there are two or maybe three possibilities. Either you had them at your home already or you obtained them from the archives at some point or maybe you had them from somewhere else, these are the three alternatives that I can see, and what the Court is asking you to indicate in respect of each of the documents on the list where you obtained that document you from. Is it clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And to be totally clear, and I will be corrected if I'm wrong, but the list contains only documents that you gave to the Defence. No? Isn't that right? Okay. Forget about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's not a complete list of the documents he handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I can explain. The list contains the provenance of the documents contained in this binder. So there is a number of documents which we received from the disclosure from the OTP from MUP, and some of the documents have been received from Mr. Bjelosevic. And he needs to pay attention only to the documents he provided to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I still don't quite understand what it was the Defence are purporting to tell us here, but it doesn't really matter. I want him to go through the documents in the binder, tell us which of them he provided, whether or not we also provided copies through our disclosure. If he provided them, where they came from in the way that His Honour Judge Harhoff has explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have no other questions, Mr. Bjelosevic, the usher will escort you out, and we would see you again on the 16th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So I'm supposed to take this with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I had two matters, I just lost one of them. Perhaps I will remember. Your Honours, the point of the matter is the following: Today on page 6, Ms. Korner -- page 6, line 7, 8, 9, and 10, Ms. Korner said: "I'm told that it was disclosed on the 1st of April 2010 in batch -- we don't know what the batch number is, it's on the CD given to the Defence on the 1st of April 2010 and it's also on EDS." Now, Your Honours, the situation is as follows: We received the batch, the disclosure batch 115 on the 23rd of March, 2010. The next batch 116 was received on the 14th of April, 2010. There was no, and I repeat, there was no disclosure on the 1st of April, 2010 neither to us nor the Zupljanin Defence, we checked. Now, the EDS has been checked at least five times. The document does not exist on the EDS. Now, what the Office of the Prosecutor provided to us is the following e-mail which we received on the 1st of April: "Counsel, Ms. Savic informed us that the documents in the attached note were not available on the EDS. Uploading them to EDS is taking longer than anticipated, so we will disclose them to you on two CDs this morning in court. Receipt of this mail will constitute proof of receipt of two CDs unless otherwise indicated." We never received these two CDs. I myself was not in the court on the 1st of April, but I'm told and I was assured a number of times that we haven't received the two discs mentioned in this -- two CDs mentioned in this mail. The same goes for the Zupljanin Defence. They have no record of receiving two discs on the 1st of April, 2010. That is all I wanted to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm really sorry to hear that, but we say they were disclosed in court. If they were not, I'm really surprised that Ms. Savic, who as you will know is considered to be the most remarkably efficient woman, did not write back saying where are the CDs you promised us. They were disclosed. The documents are in EDS. What actually happened was the request, original request from Ms. Savic saying we can't find the following list of ERNs which we wanted on EDS, will you provide them on disc. We had no obligation to do that, we did that, we gave them the disc. They never wrote back. I don't know what they did with them but that's the situation. We deny absolutely that we did not give them these CDs and we are comforted by that is that we heard from neither Defence saying they hadn't given it to us. So I hope that's the end of the matter. Your Honours, there's one other matter which is this: And can I say we will now return to the old system whereby which we had originally a physical piece of paper was handed to the Defence and they had to sign which took a long time and meant if they were in Belgrade and we were here they wouldn't get it, but if this is going to be dealt with in this way that's what's going to happen, we'll go back to the old system. The second matter is this: In terms and without any hesitation this morning, Mr. Bjelosevic said that he made and signed a statement for Mr. Cvijetic. I would now like a copy of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still maintain that I do not have that statement and that I did not take such a sort of statement from Mr. Bjelosevic. Maybe my memory is not the best but at that moment I found around 5.000 documents that I had to organise. When I return to Bijeljina, I'm going to go again through my documentation. If I find something, I'm going to bring it. But as far as I remember right now, no. I only took the most basic information that I needed at the time and I listed them the last time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And with that we take the adjournment to the 2nd of May which I trust for everybody will be not only a safe time but a time for reflection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of May, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.57 a.m.
